The provider logic now treats DeepSeek R1 model identifiers as reasoner models in both DeepSeek and OpenAI-compatible handlers, and OpenAI-compatible configurations whose base URL contains "deepseek" now use the core OpenAI client even when the URL also matches Azure.

[inference, not verified] The new branch can route an Azure-hosted DeepSeek URL through the core OpenAI client even though the adjacent code explicitly notes that Azure has a different API shape. If that endpoint still requires any AzureOpenAI-specific request or authentication behavior, requests could fail or be formed incorrectly; SDK compatibility should be verified.

[inference, not verified] Client selection now relies on the token "deepseek" appearing anywhere in the configured URL. A proxy, gateway, or unrelated host/path containing that token will also select the core OpenAI client, so the accepted URL naming invariant should be documented or tested.

hypotheses.claim: An Azure endpoint URL containing "deepseek" is routed through the core OpenAI client instead of AzureOpenAI, so endpoints that require Azure-specific authentication, API-version, or request-path semantics will fail.
hypotheses.why_suspected: The new "deepseek" condition precedes the existing "azure.com" condition and therefore wins when both match, despite the adjacent contract that Azure has a different API shape. The core-client branch also omits the Azure apiVersion configuration.
questions_to_resolve: What exact wire URL, headers, and query parameters do OpenAI and AzureOpenAI produce for an Azure-hosted DeepSeek endpoint?
Do supported Azure DeepSeek base URLs require AzureOpenAI's api-version or Azure-specific routing/authentication semantics?

hypotheses.claim: DeepSeek R1 model identifiers are detected case-sensitively, so an Azure model or deployment identifier such as "DeepSeek-R1" leaves isDeepseekReasoner false and does not receive the newly intended reasoner-specific request handling.
hypotheses.why_suspected: The added model check uses the lowercase literal "deepseek-r1" without normalizing modelId, while the constructor explicitly normalizes the base URL before matching. Azure-facing identifiers or user-defined deployment names are not shown to be normalized.
questions_to_resolve: Are openAiModelId values normalized to lowercase before reaching this handler?
What casing is used by supported Azure DeepSeek R1 model and deployment identifiers?
